title: DeWALT 18V XR 5.0Ah Power Pruner Kit - DCMPP568P1-XE $199 @ Bunnings Warehouse
body:
Deal: DeWALT 18V XR 5.0Ah Power Pruner Kit - DCMPP568P1-XE $199 @ Bunnings Warehouse

[troyww] The Ozito pole and 2.5Ah is a better deal if still available . Battery lasts all day and the pole is super handy .
Spend the extra on the $50 pruning chainsaw .
[glennp] Or $161.10 with 10% off a price match: https://www.yardworx.com.au/product/dewalt-18v-xr-power-prun…
[Hank Scorpion] I did see that one but It's a different kit (D1 = Germany vs P1 = Aus/Asia) and it has a 2ah battery, so no price match.
[LongJohn92] I got this recently from the pole saw deal. It does a great job. It would easily cut a finger or two for any Yakuza members reading this.
[unity1] When did you recieve yours? It's already 60+ days since I submitted my claim but have heard nothing.
[LongJohn92] Probably just under a month after the deal ended. I just got a random postage tracking in my AusPost app.
[Doloth] Same, have heard nothing for ages since submitting
[super hans] Same. I emailed DeWalt redemptions last week, apparently they’re out of stock and expect to send out the remaining redemption pruner orders in October
[hippyhippy] This is a great pruner… it would cut off your finger easily if you're not careful… very powerful… even thicker branches come off just have to cut a few times.. with a 2ah battery should easily last a whole day
[CH] At almost 3KG with the 5ah battery this will get heavy fast, if your pruning for more than 10 minutes I'd suggest getting/using the 2ah battery kit.
For around the same price ($213) I recommend the Kebtek KT933, it has progressive cutting and only weighs 1KG with battery
[Hank Scorpion] Isn't it 2KG for the DeWalt wtih battery, unless I'm missing something. 640g for the 5Ah battery and 1300g for the tool. But yeah, still a lot more than the one you posted.
[CH] Ah yeah you're probably right, I was just going off Bunnings page
